name: ONS household projections: 2022-based release
fact: Released 28 October 2025; 2022-based household projections are the most recent available for England, regions and local authorities and are used for planning.
gate: Projection is scenario-based, not a forecast, allocation, permission or exact parcel score.

name: ONS household projections bulletin
fact: England households are projected from 23.5m in 2022 to 25.9m in 2032 (+10.3%); Tower Hamlets has the highest local-authority 10-year household growth at 25.9%, excluding City of London.
gate: Authority demographic growth cannot be assigned to a canonical parcel without policy, capacity and geometry evidence.

name: ONS household projections methodology
fact: 2022-based household projections use 2022-based subnational population projections and assumptions derived from past demographic trends and household formation.
gate: Method supports interpretation only; it does not establish development capacity or parcel deliverability.

name: ONS subnational population projections: 2022-based release
fact: Released 24 June 2025; the latest 2022-based series provides potential population change for English local authorities and health geographies over 25 years.
gate: Population projections are contextual inputs, not allocations, permissions or parcel scores.

name: ONS subnational population projections bulletin
fact: ONS advises the migration-category variant for short-term change and states local economic development and housing policies are not included in the projections.
gate: Omitted policy/economic effects require independent local-plan and site evidence before promotion.

name: ONS subnational projections QMI
fact: QMI identifies migration, particularly local distribution of international migrants, as harder to estimate and project than fertility or mortality.
gate: Known uncertainty must be preserved; projection confidence cannot be represented as parcel certainty.

name: ONS housing affordability 2025
fact: Released 26 March 2026; provides annual house-price-to-earnings affordability ratios for national and subnational geographies in England and Wales.
gate: Affordability pressure is a demand/context signal, not evidence a parcel is developable or will grow.

name: MHCLG dwelling stock estimates England 2025
fact: Published 21 May 2026; provides dwelling-stock estimates for England and each local authority district at 31 March 2025; 2025 figures are provisional.
gate: Dwelling stock is an authority baseline and lacks parcel linkage.

name: MHCLG net additional dwellings 2024-25
fact: England recorded 208,600 net additional dwellings in 2024-25, down 6%; 190,600 were new builds and 17,710 gains from change of use.
gate: National delivery flow does not identify current land availability, allocation or parcel future-growth potential.

name: MHCLG new supply indicators Oct-Dec 2025
fact: Q4 2025 starts were 37,300 (+23% q/q), completions 36,720 (+9% q/q); estimated net additions from 1 April 2025 to 15 March 2026 were 191,300.
gate: National quarterly supply momentum is not a site pipeline, allocation, consent or parcel score.

name: MHCLG planning applications Jan-Mar 2026 release
fact: Published 19 June 2026; Accredited Official Statistics cover planning applications received, decided and granted in England.
gate: Aggregate planning activity cannot establish permission or development probability for a parcel.

name: MHCLG planning applications Jan-Mar 2026 detailed
fact: Jan-Mar 2026 district authorities received 79,600 applications, decided 68,400 and granted 59,400 (87%); 6,700 residential applications were granted.
gate: Authority totals and grant rates do not imply approval, viability or timing for any canonical parcel.

name: Housing Delivery Test collection
fact: HDT is an annual measurement of housing delivery for relevant plan-making authorities; the collection currently lists the 2023 measurement, published 12 December 2024, as latest.
gate: HDT is authority-level and the delayed publication timetable prevents treating it as a current parcel outcome.

name: Housing Delivery Test 2023 measurement
fact: The 2023 HDT covers 2020/21-2022/23; government notes a delayed publication timetable and possible combined future collections.
gate: Staleness is material; do not use the 2023 measurement as a 2026 parcel-level delivery signal.

name: Housing and economic needs assessment guidance
fact: Current guidance uses 0.8% of existing local housing stock as baseline, adjusted upward for five-year average workplace-based affordability.
gate: The standard method produces minimum annual local housing need, explicitly not a housing requirement or parcel allocation.

name: Housing supply and delivery guidance
fact: Guidance specifies 5-year supply buffers, including a defined 20% circumstance applying from 1 July 2026.
gate: Supply-buffer policy is authority/plan context and requires current plan/HDT evidence before parcel use.

name: NPPF delivering sufficient supply of homes
fact: NPPF says sufficient amount and variety of land should come forward and strategic policies should use the standard method for local housing need.
gate: National policy is not a site allocation, permission, deliverability test or exact parcel relation.

name: Planning Data local plans overview
fact: Planning Data groups national local-plan datasets including plan documents, boundaries and timetables.
gate: Structured surfaces need authoritative-source reconciliation and exact spatial/current-plan linkage before promotion.

name: Planning Data local plan dataset
fact: 1,047 local-plan records from 63 providers; collector/new data 22 July 2026; platform states MHCLG-created data pending authoritative replacement.
gate: Inventory guides discovery but origin caveat prevents authoritative parcel-policy use without source verification.

name: Planning Data plan timetable
fact: 8,927 timetable records from 73 providers; collector/new data 22 July 2026; intended to show plan-preparation stages and milestones.
gate: Milestones may change and platform origin is MHCLG-created; no adopted policy or parcel delivery timing can be inferred.

name: Planning Data development plan document
fact: 2,686 development-plan documents from one provider; collector 20 July 2026; rows link to authority documents; origin is MHCLG-created pending authoritative replacement.
gate: Linked documents must be opened and current/adopted status verified before parcel-policy extraction.

name: Planning Data brownfield land
fact: 37,666 brownfield-land records from 354 providers; collector 20 July 2026, newest data 16 July 2026; platform marks all data as authoritative-source origin.
gate: Register inclusion is a strong candidate signal, but current record, exact geometry, capacity and canonical parcel intersection remain required.

name: Planning Data infrastructure project
fact: 233 infrastructure-project records from one provider; collector 21 July 2026; boundaries inform EIA consultation and may change.
gate: Changing EIA boundaries are not confirmed construction footprints, delivery commitments or parcel uplift evidence.

name: Road Investment Strategy 3: 2026-2031
fact: Published 26 March 2026; RIS3 covers April 2026-March 2031 and sets out over £27bn for England's strategic road network, supporting growth and housing.
gate: National funding is not proof a specific scheme is funded, on schedule or creates uplift for a canonical parcel.
